notes:
Lead: Naomi Chen (AE). Mid-market SaaS — product discovery/search for SMB+ mid-market customers. Primary product is an in-app semantic search and recommendations layer for e-commerce merchants (catalogs + merchant docs).

Background / ask:
- Started with Redwood hosted API trial (Q4 2025) to validate embedding quality vs current Chroma setup. Initial eval good on relevance; Latefall now needs to prove throughput & unit economics for nightly bulk jobs and high-concurrency product pages.
- Primary goals: reduce host costs vs current self-hosted vector infra, improve recall for long-tail SKUs, maintain 50–150ms search response p95 for query+re-rank on 512-d embeddings.

Technical constraints:
- Nightly batch ingest: ~3M small docs (product + merchant metadata), target window 2–3 hours for embedding generation.
- Real-time traffic: bursty peaks up to 6k qps for search + re-ranking across 5 regional clusters. Need predictable throughput and autoscaling that doesn't blow cost.
- Currently using Postgres + Chroma (open-source) as vector DB; exploring migrations or hybrid approach (Redwood-hosted embeddings + existing DB).
- Data residency: primary US, EU for select customers — must support routing/residency and audit logs.

Security/compliance:
- Requires SSO/SAML integration for admin console, SOC2 compliance proof, KMS integration for key management, and retention controls. Legal flagged DPA/residency terms as must-have before procurement.

POC progress / conversations:
- 2026-01-15: kickoff call (ff-20260115-1a2f3b) -> AE + SE + Latefall engs. Agreed POC scope: 1) embedded quality A/B (hosted) vs Chroma, 2) batch ingest throughput test, 3) dedicated sizing run for daytime qps.
- 2026-02-12: mid-POC sync (ff-20260212-9b4c2a) -> shared early perf charts. NPS-like feedback positive on relevance. Eng note: "Hosted API returns cleaner vectors, fewer tuning iterations." — Latefall CTO (Arjun Mehta).
- 2026-02-25: demo of Dedicated features + autoscale (SE Marcus). Discussed SLA and reserved pool pricing. Customer requested detailed cost sim for 3 traffic patterns. (Drive: pricing deck).
- 2026-03-03: ran batch ingest test via hosted endpoints (POC-107). Results: 3M docs ingest took ~2.8 hours with current batch parallelism; token costs higher than target but within 15% when applying suggested batching/kv-cache tweaks. Follow-up: run with dedicated GPU pool quantized model variant for cost delta. Ticket INF-4822 opened for t-shirt sizing and connector docs.

Quotes & shorthand from meetings:
- "Quality looks 👍 but cost predictability is the blocker." — Arjun, CTO
- "If we can reduce embed cost by ~30% + guarantee ingest SLA window, we can shift to Redwood Dedicated." — Head of Product (Lena Ortiz)

Integration notes / technical asks from Latefall engs:
- Need a reference connector to keep existing Chroma DB while using Redwood embeddings (pipeline docs + examples).
- Clarify per-batch concurrency knobs and retry semantics for partial failures.
- Request a simple k/v cache strategy for top-N query reranks to reduce token counts on repeat queries.

Commercials / procurement:
- Customer prefers starting hosted (pay-as-you-go) for first 3 months while running POC, then sign 12–18 month Dedicated commit if throughput/cost targets met. Forecast: Apr 2026 close. ARR target range shared above.
